From my experience, merely running your Application on CKB Layer1 and making it a fully on-chain geek stuff sounds cool but leaves less value for those who wants to play an App with good operation experience.

recent_posts.topic_title: Introducing Myelin: a CKB-aligned off-chain Cell session runtime
recent_posts.author: ArthurZhang
recent_posts.content_text:
I offered concrete examples above, such as agent tournaments, scientific simulations, CRO/research milestones, IoT telemetry, RFQ/netting sessions.
ALSO I think you are critising a framing I did not propose. Myelin is not an attempt to make users interact with L1 directly. It sits more in the line of isomorphic L2 / ephemeral VM / court-verifiable session-runtime experiments:
keep execution off-chain
preserve CKB-shaped semantics
bring only settlement or bounded disputes back to CKB.
Application fit matters eventually, but prematurely judging the protocol by consumer UX examples misses the point. At this stage I am more interested in whether this execution/court pattern is coherent, CKB-aligned, and useful as a primitive; product packaging comes later.

recent_posts.topic_title: Spark Program | Cell Sandbox — A Visual Playground for the CKB Cell Model
recent_posts.author: zynor
recent_posts.content_text:
Hi @zz_tovarishch, and the committee,
Thank you for the feedback on the project termination. I understand the committee’s concerns about factual accuracy in educational content, and I take that seriously.
I want to respectfully address three points:
1. Work Completed and Deliverables
The approved milestones through July 4 have been fully delivered and verified:
Milestone 1 (Guided sandbox flow): Completed
Milestone 2 (Transaction inspector): Completed
Milestone 3 (partial) (Wallet integration and Build Tx): Completed
The 20% initial payment was disbursed and received. The 60% request covered work on these completed milestones. This work is live, testable, and represents significant development effort over six weeks.
The remaining 20% was appropriately held pending the final report with usability validation — a deliverable I was actively working on when the termination notice was received.
2. Factual Error Identification
I’ve conducted an audit of the educational content against CKB’s official documentation and identified terminology issues:
“Dead cell” language (non-standard terminology) — being corrected to “spent cell” to align with CKB spec
I’ve prepared fixes for these issues .
However, you mentioned “factual errors within the educational project” without specifying which ones. I would genuinely appreciate if the committee could share the specific errors you identified. This would allow me to:
Address them accurately rather than guessing
Understand where the educational content diverged from spec
Ensure all corrections are technically sound
3. Request for Fair Compensation
I’ve invested significant time in this project — from the initial MVP, through the committee feedback cycles, redesign, implementation of all three milestones, and now error correction. The work completed is substantial and was approved as delivered.
I respectfully request:
Payment for completed work (the 60% request): This represents honest effort on deliverables the committee approved on July 4
Specific error details from the committee: So I can fix them correctly
Opportunity to resubmit after corrections: The project has real educational value, and the errors are fixable
I’m committed to making Cell Sandbox a rigorous educational tool. Fair compensation for the work already done would be a meaningful way to support that continued effort.
The project is valuable. The errors are addressable. I’d like the chance to fix them properly.
Thank you for considering this respectfully.
